It is a data stealer that targets point-of-sale systems used at hotels and other businesses, and it sends collected information to a remote server. The executable is packed or encrypted to hinder analysis. The report says the initial infection vector was still undetermined.

86e496f986f55f6c0b0191ce30111a6769ca7696.summary: S2W analysis of a 2020 watering-hole attack on a North Korea-related website, visited by users of an older Internet Explorer. Multi-stage Ruby and PE loaders decrypt a final payload, a variant of ROKRAT that steals files, browser and mail data, takes screenshots and logs keys. It uses legitimate cloud services (pCloud, Yandex, Box, Dropbox, Backblaze B2) for command and control. The report judges the activity to be related to Scarcruft (APT37, Group123), which it describes as linked to North Korea and active since 2012.

86dcb88e8ad174d9169c965836b00c32697ebb17.summary: AhnLab ASEC describes a campaign called KONO DIO DA that targets poorly managed Linux SSH servers through dictionary attacks. It installs XMRig CoinMiner under a disguised process name, drops SHC-built downloader scripts, and creates a backdoor SSH account. Past cases also used a planted SSH key, cron persistence and disabled security tools. The report recommends strong, changed passwords, patching, firewalls and updating the V3 product.

86386937e41bf38b9841e7283909aa36d152dc14.summary: ESET, working with CERT-UA, analysed a destructive attack on a Ukrainian energy provider in April 2022. The attackers used Industroyer2, a new variant of the 2016 Industroyer ICS malware, to cut power in a region, alongside CaddyWiper and Linux and Solaris wipers. ESET assesses with high confidence that the Sandworm group is responsible. The report says how the attackers got in and moved to the ICS network is not yet known.

86fa5c6b040131cf4345d0904ab05251cc387246.summary: IronNet reports botnets and cryptominer operators rapidly exploiting Atlassian Confluence CVE-2021-26084 after an August 2021 patch and public proof-of-concept code. The report calls most activity financially motivated, but judges that more sophisticated actors likely use the exploit for intelligence collection.

86b8c909afd63ec436249037400dd59428798f1d.summary: Sucuri blog post (February 2016) on a WordPress infection that injects encrypted JavaScript into legitimate .js files and loads a hidden iframe ad page. The report calls it the admedia iframe injection. Its malicious subdomains were registered under one name and point to DigitalOcean servers. It describes domain shadowing, cross-site contamination across shared hosting, and constant reinfection through backdoors left on the server.
